questions.q: Which statement is an example of business lineage, per this lesson?
options: "Customer Lifetime Value on the executive dashboard comes from the CRM and the billing system"
"dbo.CLV_Summary.LifetimeValueUSD is computed in sp_CalculateCLV by summing Billing.Invoices.AmountPaid"
"The server has 64 gigabytes of RAM"
"The nightly job runs at 2 AM Eastern time"
questions.explain: Business lineage uses plain domain terms and system names, without specific tables, columns, or code — exactly the level a non-technical stakeholder needs.

questions.q: Who is technical lineage primarily built for, according to this lesson?
options: Data engineers and analysts who need to trace a bug or assess a schema change at the table/column level
Customers browsing a company's public website
Marketing teams designing a new logo
Executives who never look at a query editor
questions.explain: Technical lineage is precise enough — specific tables, columns, and transformation logic — for someone doing hands-on debugging or impact analysis.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what happens if an organization maintains only technical lineage and no business lineage?
options: Business stakeholders can't answer basic trust questions themselves and every 'where does this come from' becomes a ticket to the data team
The organization saves money because technical lineage is cheaper to maintain
Engineers lose the ability to perform root cause analysis entirely
Regulatory audits become easier because detail is already maximized
questions.explain: Without a business-level view, non-technical stakeholders have no self-service way to understand where a number comes from, creating extra work for the data team.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend as the relationship between the business and technical lineage views, in a mature practice?
options: The business view is usually generated as a simplified roll-up of the technical one, rather than maintained as separate, unrelated documentation
They should be built by completely different teams with no shared source of truth
Only one of the two views should ever be created, depending on company size
The technical view should be hidden from all engineers for security reasons
questions.explain: Mature lineage practices keep one underlying truth and derive the readable business summary from the detailed technical lineage, instead of maintaining two disconnected sets of documentation.

questions.q: According to the lesson's 'quick test,' what tells you a lineage diagram is showing technical lineage rather than business lineage?
options: The boxes are named with specific object names like dbo.Accounts or sp_CalculateCLV instead of plain system names like "CRM"
The diagram uses more colors than a business lineage diagram
The diagram was drawn by an executive rather than an engineer
The diagram contains no boxes at all, only arrows
questions.explain: Technical lineage diagrams use specific table, column, or job names; business lineage diagrams use plain domain and system names instead.
